venue: FENWAY PARK (4 Jersey Street, Boston, MA). CONFIRMED CURRENT for the 2026 season, checked 16 August 2026. NO RENAME AND NO RELOCATION: (1) RateYourSeats event listings fetched 16 Aug 2026 from the Fenway Park section pages show the 2026 Red Sox home schedule at this venue - verbatim: 'Aug 17 Mon 7:10pm Arizona Diamondbacks at Boston Red Sox', 'Aug 21 Fri 7:10pm San Francisco Giants at Boston Red Sox', 'Aug 31 Mon 6:45pm Seattle Mariners at Boston Red Sox' (25 upcoming events listed) - https://www.rateyourseats.com/fenway-park/seating/sections/FB1 . (2) Ballparks of Baseball states verbatim: '-Naming Rights: None - Named after the nearby location of The Fens' and '-Tenant: Boston Red Sox' - https://www.ballparksofbaseball.com/ballparks/fenway-park/ . Fenway Park has NEVER sold stadium naming rights, so the Daikin Park / Rate Field class of error CANNOT occur here; there is no stadium naming right to go stale. (3) MLB.com's own Fenway Park guide, published 18 March 2026, still titles the building 'Fenway Park' - https://www.mlb.com/news/featured/fenway-park-guide-capacity-seating-chart-parking-and-more . (4) Wikipedia: opened, verbatim, 'The first game was played April 20, 1912' - https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fenway_Park . FIELD-NAMING-RIGHT DISTINCTION (the UNIQLO/Dodger Stadium trap): no field naming right was found at Fenway either. BUT sponsor names on INTERIOR SEATING AREAS DO change and several ARE STALE in the ticketing source - see 'uncertain'. Confirmed 2026 interior renames: the club level formerly 'State Street Pavilion Club' is now 'AURA PAVILION CLUB' (RateYourSeats' own section INDEX still prints the stale label 'State Street Pavilion Club 1' while the individual section page it links to is headed 'Aura Pavilion Club 1 at Fenway Park' - https://www.rateyourseats.com/fenway-park/seating/sections/PC1 ); and the club whose URL slug is still the legacy 'EMCC' (EMC Club) is now the 'DELL TECHNOLOGIES CLUB', whose review text calls the sections 'DTC 1-DTC 6' - https://www.rateyourseats.com/fenway-park/seating/dell-technologies-club .
concert_only_sections: NOTE ON THESE FOUR ENTRIES: they appear in the RateYourSeats Fenway Park section index (https://www.rateyourseats.com/fenway-park/seating/sections) as links but have NO per-section page - each points at a ZONE page, so there is no individual section identifier behind them and they MUST NOT be emitted as sections. 'Field Sections' -> /fenway-park/seating/field-seats is the CONCERT FLOOR laid on the playing surface and is not a baseball section at all. 'Hornitos Cantina' -> /fenway-park/seating/hornitos-cantina IS a real baseball standing/ledge area, not a concert-only area, but has no per-section page; verbatim: 'Right Field Cantina Seating: Located along the right field line underneath the Grandstand overhang', it offers 'barstools and ledge seating' and sits 'behind the traditional Grandstand seating sections' with 'support poles'. 'Roof Deck Tables' and 'Roof Deck SRO' BOTH link to the single zone page /fenway-park/seating/right-field-roof-deck; both are real baseball ticket types ('Each table includes four seats arranged around a shared table' and SRO giving 'access to standing space near the main Roof Deck bar area') but neither resolves to a numbered section. They are listed here ONLY because the brief directs zone links with no per-section page to this key; three of the four are baseball areas, NOT concert-floor sections.

SEPARATE WARNING - CONCERT RECONFIGURATION: many ordinary baseball sections are flagged on their own pages as concert-obstructed, e.g. verbatim from https://www.rateyourseats.com/fenway-park/seating/sections/FB1 : 'Field Box 1 is behind the stage or to the side of the stage for most concerts. This may restrict or limit your view of the performance.' Identical wording appears on B34 and B43. These ARE baseball sections and remain in 'sections'.
capacity: CONFLICTING FIGURES - FOUR DIFFERENT NUMBERS FOUND, NO TWO SOURCES AGREE. (a) 37,775 - MLB.com's own Fenway Park guide, article dated 18 March 2026, verbatim: 'Capacity: 37,775' - https://www.mlb.com/news/featured/fenway-park-guide-capacity-seating-chart-parking-and-more . (b) 37,755 (night) - Wikipedia infobox; Wikipedia adds that the day figure varies because the centre-field bleachers are tarped to form the batter's eye: 'Center field contains bleachers that are tarped off during day games' - https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fenway_Park . (c) 37,673 (night) and 37,221 (day) - Ballparks of Baseball, verbatim: '-Capacity: 37,673 (night), 37,221 (day)' - https://www.ballparksofbaseball.com/ballparks/fenway-park/ . RECOMMENDED: 37,775, because it is the only figure from the club's own family of sites AND the only one carrying a 2026 publication date. RECORD ALSO that Fenway is one of the few parks with a GENUINE NIGHT-vs-DAY capacity difference (centre-field bleachers tarped for the batter's eye by day), so a single scalar capacity is intrinsically approximate here.

orientation.batter_faces: NORTHEAST. Where's The Shade, verbatim: the park faces 'northeast', and 'the sun rises behind right field and tracks across the first-base side and outfield for much of the afternoon' - https://wherestheshade.com/stadium/fenway-park . Home plate to centre field therefore runs to the NORTHEAST; RIGHT FIELD is the EAST/SOUTH-EAST side of the park (the sun comes up behind it) and LEFT FIELD / the Green Monster is the NORTH-WEST side.
orientation.sun_and_shade: Shade arrives from the THIRD BASE side first and the FIRST BASE / right-field side bakes longest. Where's The Shade, verbatim: 'Shade doesn't arrive evenly, rather it creeps in from the third-base side first' and the Green Monster and right-field bleachers get 'full exposure during day games, with little relief until very late in the afternoon' - https://wherestheshade.com/stadium/fenway-park . RateYourSeats' Field Boxes zone page agrees: the Third Base Side 'Receives shade earlier in the day' while the First Base Side 'Typically stays in the sun longer during day games' - https://www.rateyourseats.com/fenway-park/seating/field-boxes . RateYourSeats' Right Field Boxes page: these seats 'tend to stay in the sun longer than most other seating areas at Fenway Park. Aside from the Bleachers, they are often the last sections in the stadium to move into the shade during afternoon games.' - https://www.rateyourseats.com/fenway-park/seating/right-field-boxes .
orientation.confidence: MEDIUM-HIGH. Only one source gives a compass word ('northeast'), but it is independently corroborated by TWO unrelated sun/shade descriptions (third-base side shades first; right field is last to shade) which are only consistent with a north-easterly orientation, and by the physical fact that the Green Monster is in left field on the Lansdowne Street side. No source gives degrees. Baseball Almanac's AL orientation page renders its Fenway value only as a compass GRAPHIC, not as text, so it could not be quoted - https://www.baseball-almanac.com/stadium/ballpark_NSEW_AL.shtml .
orientation.geometry_cross_check: Corroborated by the official accessibility guide's elevator geography, which is among the hardest facts available: Gate B's elevator serves 'the Right Field Grandstand, Right Field Roof Deck, Right Field Roof Box areas' while Gate E's serves 'the left field grandstand, Green Monster' - https://www.mlb.com/redsox/ballpark/disability-access-guide . Right-field and left-field structures are therefore on opposite sides of the building as described.

numbering_direction.summary: *** FENWAY PARK USES TWO DIFFERENT AND INCOMPATIBLE NUMBERING SYSTEMS IN THE SAME BUILDING. READ BOTH. *** (A) The LOWER TIERS (Field Box, Right Field Box, Loge Box, Grandstand, Bleachers) SWEEP CONTINUOUSLY: section numbers INCREASE FROM THE FIRST-BASE / RIGHT-FIELD SIDE, PAST HOME PLATE, TOWARD THE THIRD-BASE / LEFT-FIELD SIDE. On a standard chart drawn with home plate at the bottom and first base to the right, that sweep runs CLOCKWISE. (B) The PAVILION / ROOF TIERS (Aura Pavilion Club PC, Pavilion Box PB, Pavilion Reserved PR, Roof Box RB) DO NOT SWEEP AT ALL - THEY NUMBER OUTWARD FROM HOME PLATE BY PARITY: ODD numbers run down the FIRST BASE line, EVEN numbers run down the THIRD BASE line. *** THIS IS THE PARITY SIGNATURE THE BRIEF WARNS ABOUT, AND AT FENWAY IT APPLIES TO ONLY PART OF THE PARK. A generator config that carries a single park-wide 'direction' scalar WILL BE WRONG FOR FENWAY: the schema must permit a per-tier choice between 'sweep' and 'parity'. ***
numbering_direction.system_A_sweep_direction: INCREASES from RIGHT FIELD / FIRST BASE toward LEFT FIELD / THIRD BASE (clockwise on a standard chart).

system_A_anchors_lower_level_field_box.right_field_anchor: FB1 through roughly FB9 are in RIGHT FIELD down the first base line. The RateYourSeats expert review block printed on the Field Box 1 page is the RIGHT FIELD BOXES review, verbatim: 'Main Level Right Field Seating: Located on the lower level down the first base line near right field.' and, in the same block, 'seats in Section 5 look more directly toward right field' - https://www.rateyourseats.com/fenway-park/seating/sections/FB1 . INDEPENDENT OFFICIAL CORROBORATION: the Red Sox netting page names Field Box Section 9 as the first-base-side END of the netting run (see below).
system_A_anchors_lower_level_field_box.home_plate_anchor: FB39-FB50 are DIRECTLY BEHIND HOME PLATE. THREE INDEPENDENT SOURCES: (1) RateYourSeats Dugout Club zone page, verbatim: 'Sections 39-50 (Rows A1-3)' sit directly behind home plate - https://www.rateyourseats.com/fenway-park/seating/dugout-club . (2) The Field Box 45 section page places it 'directly behind home plate' - https://www.rateyourseats.com/fenway-park/seating/sections/FB45 . (3) RateYourSeats' shaded/covered page, verbatim: 'Upper rows of Field Boxes 39-50' are the field boxes that fall into shade for 1:00 p.m. games - https://www.rateyourseats.com/fenway-park/seating/shaded-covered-seats (the behind-the-plate band is exactly what shades first at a north-east-facing park).
system_A_anchors_lower_level_field_box.left_field_anchor: FB79-FB82 are at the THIRD BASE / LEFT FIELD end. OFFICIAL: the Red Sox netting page, verbatim: 'The protective netting at Fenway Park extends from Field Box Section 79 to Field Box Section 9.' - https://www.mlb.com/redsox/ballpark/netting . Section 79 is the third-base end of that run and Section 9 the first-base end. CORROBORATION: Where's The Shade lists the third-base-side shaded field boxes as 'Field Boxes Sections F47-F82 (upper rows)' - https://wherestheshade.com/stadium/fenway-park .
system_A_anchors_lower_level_field_box.dugout_cross_check: RateYourSeats Field Boxes zone page, verbatim: 'Sections 21-28 sit behind the Red Sox dugout, while Sections 62-68 are behind the visitor dugout.' - https://www.rateyourseats.com/fenway-park/seating/field-boxes . Per-section confirmation: FB21 - 'These seats are located behind the Red Sox dugout' (https://www.rateyourseats.com/fenway-park/seating/sections/FB21 ); FB62 - 'For baseball games, these seats are located behind the visitor dugout' (https://www.rateyourseats.com/fenway-park/seating/sections/FB62 ). Because the Red Sox (home) dugout is on the FIRST BASE side, the LOW numbers sit on the first base side. THIS IS THE LOAD-BEARING CROSS-CHECK: it is derived from dugout identity, not from a stadium-guide narrative, and it agrees with the official netting endpoints.

numbering_direction.system_A_anchors_loge_level: FULLY EXPLICIT ON ONE PAGE - the cleanest three-anchor set in the park. RateYourSeats Loge Boxes zone page, verbatim: 'First Base Side (Sections 98-106)'; 'Sections 125-134 behind home plate provide some of the best sightlines in the ballpark.'; 'Third Base Side (Sections 157-165)' - https://www.rateyourseats.com/fenway-park/seating/loge-boxes . Per-section confirmation: LB98 is described as on the first base side with 'a head-on view of the Green Monster' (https://www.rateyourseats.com/fenway-park/seating/sections/LB98 ); LB165 is 'situated on the third base side' and 'receives shade earlier in the day' (https://www.rateyourseats.com/fenway-park/seating/sections/LB165 ); LB130 is 'Behind home plate on the Loge Level' (https://www.rateyourseats.com/fenway-park/seating/sections/LB130 ). Where's The Shade independently gives the behind-the-plate loge band as 'Loge Boxes Sections B125-B136 (upper rows)' - https://wherestheshade.com/stadium/fenway-park .
numbering_direction.system_A_anchors_grandstand: GS1-GS6 = FIRST BASE / right-field side; GS18-GS20 = behind home plate; GS23-GS33 = THIRD BASE / left-field side. Sources: RateYourSeats Grandstand zone page, verbatim: 'Sections 1-6 are covered but can still receive late afternoon sun' - the late-afternoon-sun side at Fenway is the FIRST BASE side per the shade sources above - https://www.rateyourseats.com/fenway-park/seating/grandstand-seats . Where's The Shade lists the third-base-side shaded grandstand as 'Grandstand Sections 23-33 (higher rows)' - https://wherestheshade.com/stadium/fenway-park . The GS33 section page places it in the left field corner next to the Green Monster, and the shaded/covered page notes 'All Grandstand sections (except GS33)' are covered - GS33 is the one grandstand section the roof does not reach, which is the far left-field end - https://www.rateyourseats.com/fenway-park/seating/shaded-covered-seats . The GS20 page places that section behind home plate on the infield - https://www.rateyourseats.com/fenway-park/seating/sections/GS20 . CONFIDENCE: direction HIGH; the exact behind-the-plate grandstand section NUMBERS are MEDIUM - see 'uncertain'.
numbering_direction.system_A_anchors_bleachers: The bleacher run CONTINUES the same clockwise sweep past the Green Monster: B34 is the CENTRE / left-centre end (adjacent to the batter's eye) and B43 is the RIGHT FIELD end. Sources: the Bleachers 43 page carries the insight, verbatim: 'The Visiting Team Bullpen is in Front of Bleachers Sections 42 and 43' - the Fenway bullpens are in right / right-centre field - https://www.rateyourseats.com/fenway-park/seating/sections/B43 . Wikipedia independently fixes the high end in right field, verbatim: the red seat is 'Located in Section 42, Row 37, Seat 21 in right field bleachers', marking Ted Williams' 502-foot home run - https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fenway_Park . Wikipedia also places the low end at centre: 'Center field contains bleachers that are tarped off during day games' (the batter's eye, i.e. the B34-B35 end).
numbering_direction.system_B_parity_tiers: *** PARITY SIGNATURE, STATED LOUDLY. *** RateYourSeats Aura Club & Aura Pavilion zone page, verbatim: 'Aura Club Sections (AC1-AC5) - Located directly behind home plate'; 'Aura Pavilion Sections (AP1-AP14) - Extend down the baselines'; and decisively: 'Odd-numbered sections run along the first base line' while 'Even-numbered sections run along the third base line' - https://www.rateyourseats.com/fenway-park/seating/aura-club-aura-pavilion . Per-section confirmation: the PC1 page ('Aura Pavilion Club 1') is on the first base side and the PC2 page ('Aura Pavilion Club 2') states 'Even-numbered sections run along the third base line' - https://www.rateyourseats.com/fenway-park/seating/sections/PC1 and .../PC2 . THE SAME PARITY RULE IS INDEPENDENTLY CORROBORATED ON THE PAVILION BOX AND ROOF BOX SERIES BY TWO SUN/SHADE SOURCES THAT NEVER MENTION PARITY: (i) Where's The Shade lists the THIRD-BASE-side shaded pavilion boxes as 'Pavilion Boxes Sections PB2-PB14' - ALL EVEN - https://wherestheshade.com/stadium/fenway-park ; (ii) RateYourSeats' shaded/covered page names the two pavilion boxes that DO catch sun as 'Pavilion Boxes 11 & 13' - BOTH ODD, i.e. both on the sunnier first base side - https://www.rateyourseats.com/fenway-park/seating/shaded-covered-seats . (iii) PAVILION RESERVED follows it exactly: 'Section 15' (odd) is 'Located on the first base side of the field' while 'Sections 16-20' (even) are 'Located on the third base side of the field' - https://www.rateyourseats.com/fenway-park/seating/pavilion-reserved . Note PR17 and PR19 DO NOT EXIST in the index, which is exactly what parity predicts if the first-base pavilion run simply ends. (iv) ROOF BOX exists ONLY in ODD numbers 23,25,27,29,31,33,35,37,39,41,43 and the zone page places them 'along the first base line on the top deck of Fenway Park' - https://www.rateyourseats.com/fenway-park/seating/right-field-roof-boxes . An odd-only series that is entirely on the first base side is precisely what the odd=first-base parity rule predicts; the even counterparts 24-42 would fall on the third base side, where the Green Monster leaves no room for a roof box, so they are simply absent.
numbering_direction.does_the_park_sweep_one_way_round_the_bo: PARTIALLY. The lower bowl DOES sweep one way (clockwise, first base -> home -> third base) and its four series chain together geographically: Field Box 1-82 runs right field -> home -> left field corner, then Grandstand 1-33 repeats the same arc one tier back, then Bleachers 34-43 carry the Grandstand series onward from centre field to right field. But the pavilion/roof tiers ABANDON the sweep for parity. DO NOT MODEL FENWAY WITH A SINGLE PARK-WIDE DIRECTION.
numbering_direction.numbering_discontinuity_warning: The RIGHT FIELD BOX series (RFB87-RFB97) BREAKS the lower-bowl sweep. Those eleven sections are physically in RIGHT FIELD, adjacent to the LOW-numbered Field Boxes (FB1-FB9), yet they carry numbers ABOVE the highest Field Box (FB82, which is at the opposite, left-field end of the park). Verbatim: 'Right Field Box sections are located on the main seating level down the first base line toward right field' and 'On the Fenway Park seating chart, these sections appear adjacent to the Field Box and Loge Box areas' - https://www.rateyourseats.com/fenway-park/seating/right-field-boxes . A generator that assumes 'higher number = further round the bowl' will place RFB87-97 in LEFT field. It must not. Numbers 83-86 are absent from the index entirely. Which END of the RFB run is nearer the infield (87 or 97) is NOT STATED by any source found - see 'uncertain'.
numbering_direction.number_reuse_warning: *** PLAIN NUMBERS ARE REUSED ACROSS TIERS AT FENWAY AND ARE AMBIGUOUS WITHOUT THE ZONE PREFIX. *** Sections 1-14 exist simultaneously as Field Box, Grandstand, Monster Seats, Aura Pavilion Club, Pavilion Box and Dell Technologies Club sections; sections 34-43 exist simultaneously as Field Box, Bleachers and Roof Box. A bare '42' at Fenway could be Field Box 42 (behind home plate) or Bleachers 42 (the red seat, 502 feet away in right field). The RateYourSeats section IDENTIFIERS recorded in 'sections' (FB42 vs B42) are the disambiguated form and MUST be carried through the pipeline intact.

home_plate_sections.Right Field Box: NONE - this tier never wraps behind the plate; it is entirely down the first base line in right field. Omit the anchor; distances from this tier must come out blank, not wrong.
home_plate_sections.Bleachers: NONE - this tier never wraps behind the plate; it is entirely in centre and right field beyond the outfield wall. Omit the anchor.
home_plate_sections.Monster Seats: NONE - this tier never wraps behind the plate; it sits atop the left field wall, 'directly above the left field wall' approximately 37 feet up. Omit the anchor.
home_plate_sections.Roof Box: NONE - odd-numbered only, entirely 'along the first base line on the top deck'. Omit the anchor.
home_plate_sections.Aura Pavilion Club (PC) / Pavilion Box (: NONE IN THE USUAL SENSE - these are PARITY series that begin ADJACENT to home plate and run OUTWARD down the two foul lines. The lowest numbers (PC1/PC2, PB1/PB2) are the closest to home plate but sit on the first-base (odd) and third-base (even) sides respectively rather than squarely behind the plate. The squarely-behind-the-plate seats on this level are the separate HPPC/Aura Club series. Do not assign a single centre anchor to PC/PB/PR.

Loge: 'Sections 125-134 behind home plate provide some of the best sightlines in the ballpark.' - https://www.rateyourseats.com/fenway-park/seating/loge-boxes . levels.name: Field Box (lower level, incl. Dugout Club and Jim Beam Dugout rows)
levels.notes: The main lower bowl, in front of the Grandstand. Sweeps clockwise: FB1-FB9 right field / first base line, FB21-FB28 behind the Red Sox (home) dugout, FB39-FB50 directly behind home plate, FB62-FB68 behind the visitor dugout, FB79-FB82 the third base / left field end. Verbatim: 'These sections typically sit within 20 rows of the playing field', are 'positioned in front of the Grandstand' with 'no support poles obstruct[ing]' views, and 'All seats in these sections sit behind protective netting, which extends across the infield to help protect fans from foul balls.' Rows: 'Rows in the Field Box sections are labeled with letters, generally running from the front rows up to Row M, where the main concourse walkway is located.' The front-most rows of certain Field Box sections are sold as DUGOUT CLUB: 'Sections 39-50 (Rows A1-3)', 'Sections 29-38 and 51-61 (Rows 1-2)', 'Sections 17-20 (Rows 1-2)' near the camera wells, and 'Sections 13-16 and 72-79 (Rows 1-2)'. The JIM BEAM DUGOUT is 'located next to the Red Sox dugout at field level' and 'positioned below field level, similar to a real baseball dugout' - i.e. first base side.

levels.name: Right Field Box
levels.notes: Same physical deck as the Field Boxes but out in right field, and numbered OUT OF SEQUENCE with them (see numbering_direction.numbering_discontinuity_warning). Verbatim: 'Located on the lower level down the first base line near right field'; 'Budget-Friendly Lower Level Seats: Often the cheapest unobstructed tickets on the main level of Fenway Park.'; 'Many seats face toward the outfield rather than toward the infield' and fans 'often need to turn their body to follow the action around home plate'; 'Because they sit in front of the Grandstand seating, Right Field Box seats still offer unobstructed views, avoiding the support poles that affect some other areas of the ballpark.'; 'Full Sun Exposure: These sections are uncovered and among the last seats in the ballpark to receive shade.'

levels.name: Loge Box
levels.sections: LB98-LB165, EXCEPT LB156 which is absent from the index
levels.notes: Directly behind and above the Field Boxes, in front of the Grandstand. Verbatim: 'Located on the Loge Level directly behind the Field Boxes, offering a great viewing height near the action.' and, of the behind-the-plate band, all seats 'sit in front of Grandstand support poles' giving 'unobstructed views'. Anchors, verbatim: 'First Base Side (Sections 98-106)', 'Sections 125-134 behind home plate', 'Third Base Side (Sections 157-165)'. Rows: 'Each Loge section typically contains fewer than 15 rows, with rows labeled AA through NN.' - but individual sections start at different letters (LB98 is DD-RR, LB130 is AA-NN, LB165 is JJ-PP), so the AA-NN statement is a generalisation, NOT a per-section truth.

levels.name: Grandstand
levels.notes: The original 1912-era covered tier, behind the Loge Boxes. Verbatim: 'Grandstand seating wraps around much of the lower seating bowl at Fenway Park, sitting directly beneath the large roof structure that covers much of the stadium.' Split into 'Grandstand Infield and Grandstand Outfield'. THE HIGH-OBSTRUCTION TIER: 'Support poles positioned throughout the sections can block views of different parts of the field, including home plate, the pitcher's mound, second base, or the outfield, depending on the seat location.' and 'support poles and tight seating layouts were common design features at the time and remain part of the Grandstand experience today.' 'Grandstand seats on the third base side generally offer better sightlines than those on the first base side'. Covered: 'All Grandstand sections (except GS33)'. Rows are NUMBERED (1-18 or 1-19 depending on section).

levels.name: Bleachers
levels.notes: Beyond the outfield wall, continuing the Grandstand number series. Verbatim: 'Bleacher sections are located in right field and right-center field at Fenway Park.' B34 is the centre-field end (its rows run only 1-10 and Wikipedia notes 'Center field contains bleachers that are tarped off during day games' to form the batter's eye); B42-B43 are the right-field end, with 'The Visiting Team Bullpen is in Front of Bleachers Sections 42 and 43'. Rows are NUMBERED and run very deep in the middle of the run: B42 and B43 are 'labeled 1-50', B40 is 'labeled 1-19', B34 is 'labeled 1-10'. No shade: the shaded/covered guide records bleacher sections 34-43 as having no shade coverage, and a fan advises 'Avoid the bleachers at all costs for late afternoon and evening games if you are sensitive to the sun.'

levels.name: Green Monster Seats
levels.notes: Atop the left field wall. Verbatim: 'This seating area runs along the top of the wall and is divided into several sections labeled M1 through M10 on the Boston Red Sox seating chart.'; the seats sit 'directly above the left field wall' at approximately 37 feet; 'Sections M2 through M6 are particularly desirable for fans hoping to catch a home run ball, as they sit near the most common landing areas for balls cleared over the wall.' Two ticket types: 'Reserved Green Monster Seats' (individual barstools with drink rails) and 'Standing Room Only (SRO) Monster Tickets' which 'allow fans access to the Green Monster walkway'. Rows are NUMBERED and very shallow - 'Rows in Monster Seats 1 are labeled 1-3'. Ballparks of Baseball: 'approximately 250 Green Monster Seats were added atop the left-field wall' before 2003. WHICH END OF THE WALL M1 SITS AT IS NOT STATED BY ANY SOURCE FOUND.

levels.name: Dell Technologies Club (URL slug EMCC = legacy 'EMC Club')
levels.sections: EMCC1-EMCC6 (called 'DTC 1-DTC 6' in the current review text)
levels.notes: Verbatim: 'Dell Technologies Club seating includes sections DTC 1-DTC 6, located directly behind home plate on the second level above the Grandstand seating at Fenway Park.' Amenities, verbatim: 'Padded seats with extra legroom and full overhead coverage'; 'In-Seat Wait Service (Red Sox Games)'; 'Access to an exclusive restaurant and lounge space'; 'Three full-service bars'; 'Climate-controlled indoor dining space'. Fully covered. The index label and the URL slug are STALE - see 'uncertain'.

levels.name: Aura Club / Home Plate Pavilion Club (URL slug HPPC)
levels.sections: HPPC1-HPPC5 (called 'AC1-AC5' in the current review text)
levels.notes: Verbatim: 'Aura Club Sections (AC1-AC5) - Located directly behind home plate'. Highest tier, under the roof.

levels.name: Aura Pavilion Club (URL slug PC; index label still 'State Street Pavilion Club' - STALE)
levels.sections: PC1-PC14 (called 'AP1-AP14' in the current review text)
levels.notes: PARITY TIER. Verbatim: 'Aura Pavilion Sections (AP1-AP14) - Extend down the baselines'; 'Odd-numbered sections run along the first base line'; 'Even-numbered sections run along the third base line'. Rows: 'Each section contains five rows of seating labeled Rows 1-5.' and 'In Row 5, seats are replaced with a barstool-style setup positioned along a ledge'.

levels.name: Pavilion Box
levels.notes: PARITY TIER (odd = first base side, even = third base side; corroborated by two independent shade sources - see numbering_direction.system_B_parity_tiers). row_seat_conventions: ROW LABELLING VARIES BY TIER AND, CRITICALLY, VARIES SECTION-BY-SECTION WITHIN A TIER. DO NOT APPLY A SINGLE ROW SCHEME PER LEVEL. Verified per tier: (1) FIELD BOX - LETTERED rows, but with irregular prefixes on the premium front rows. Zone statement, verbatim: 'Rows in the Field Box sections are labeled with letters, generally running from the front rows up to Row M, where the main concourse walkway is located.' Observed per-section: FB1 'labeled A-N'; FB21 and FB62 'labeled A-M'; FB80 'labeled AAA, A-L'; FB82 'labeled D-L'; FB45 'labeled A1, 2-3, A-M'. NOTE FB45's 'A1, 2-3' and FB80's 'AAA' - these are the Dugout Club front rows, which use NUMERIC or triple-letter labels sitting IN FRONT of Row A. The Dugout Club zone page confirms: 'Sections 39-50 (Rows A1-3)' and other Dugout Club ranges use '(Rows 1-2)'. So a single Field Box section can contain both numeric and lettered rows, with the numeric ones FIRST. (2) RIGHT FIELD BOX - DOUBLE-LETTERED rows: RFB87 'labeled DD-XX'; RFB97 'labeled BB-XX' with 'An entrance to this section is located at Row BB'. (3) LOGE BOX - DOUBLE-LETTERED rows. Zone statement, verbatim: 'Each Loge section typically contains fewer than 15 rows, with rows labeled AA through NN.' Observed per-section, and DIFFERENT from the zone claim: LB98 'labeled DD-RR'; LB130 'labeled AA-NN'; LB165 'labeled JJ-PP'. The zone statement is a generalisation only. Zone note: 'section entrances are positioned at Row AA'. (4) GRANDSTAND - NUMBERED rows. GS1 'labeled 1-18'; GS18 'labeled 1-18' with 'An entrance to this section is located at Row 18'; GS20 'labeled 1-18'; GS15 'labeled 1-19' with an entrance at Row 19; GS33 'labeled 1-15' with 'An entrance to this section is located at Row 15'. Row 1 is the FRONT row and is repeatedly singled out as the only unobstructed row. (5) BLEACHERS - NUMBERED rows, of wildly differing depth: B34 'labeled 1-10'; B40 'labeled 1-19'; B42 'labeled 1-50'; B43 'labeled 1-50' with 'An entrance to this section is located at Row 6'. (6) GREEN MONSTER SEATS - NUMBERED rows, very shallow: M1 'labeled 1-3'. (7) AURA PAVILION CLUB (PC) - NUMBERED rows: 'Each section contains five rows of seating labeled Rows 1-5' and 'In Row 5, seats are replaced with a barstool-style setup positioned along a ledge'. PC2 has 'An entrance to this section is located at Row 5'. (8) PAVILION BOX (PB) - LETTERED rows A-E: 'Rows in Pavilion Box 1 are labeled A-E'; 'Each section typically contains fewer than five rows of seating, with Row A located closest to the front of the section.' (9) PAVILION RESERVED (PR) - LETTERED rows: 'Each Pavilion Reserved section contains 10 rows of seating, with Row A located at the front of the section.' (10) RIGHT FIELD ROOF BOX (RB) - LETTERED rows: 'Each section includes eight rows labeled A through G' (INTERNALLY CONTRADICTORY - eight rows cannot be labelled with the seven letters A-G; see 'uncertain'). (11) SRO AREAS - no rows: 'Seats and rows are not assigned and are first-come, first-serve.' ACCESSIBLE-ROW LABEL CONVENTION: UNKNOWN - no source states one. SEATS PER ROW, verbatim from the seating-chart page: 'Lower Level infield sections especially near behind home plate have more seats typically ranging around 25 to 30 seats. Upper deck level sections near behind home plate have typically only about 10 to 15 seats in total. The outfield seats in right field range from as little as 10 seats to 30 seats depending on which section you are in. The Green Monster in left typically have less than 10 seats in each section.' - https://www.rateyourseats.com/fenway-park/seating/seating-chart
seat1_side_verbatim: *** TWO SOURCES ON THE SAME SITE FLATLY CONTRADICT EACH OTHER. BOTH ARE RECORDED. THEY ARE NOT RECONCILED. *** (A) THE PER-SECTION BOILERPLATE. Quoted EXACTLY as printed, including the site's duplicated word 'field': "When looking towards the field/field/stage, lower number seats are on the left". This sentence appeared VERBATIM AND IDENTICALLY on EVERY individual section page fetched, with no variation and no per-section override anywhere: https://www.rateyourseats.com/fenway-park/seating/sections/ FB1, FB21, FB45, FB62, FB80, FB82, RFB87, RFB97, LB98, LB130, LB165, GS1, GS15, GS18, GS20, GS33, B34, B40, B42, B43, M1, PB1, PB2, PC1, PC2 - twenty-five pages spanning the right field lower bowl, behind home plate, the third base side, the left field grandstand, the bleachers, the Green Monster and both parity tiers. Read literally, this places SEAT 1 ON THE LEFT as you face the field. NOTE: one render of the FB1 page printed the same sentence with a single 'field' - "When looking towards the field/stage, lower number seats are on the left" - the directional claim is identical. (B) THE PARK-WIDE STATEMENT ON THE SEATING-CHART PAGE, which says the OPPOSITE, verbatim: "Seat Numbers at Fenway Park go from right-to-left. When seated looking at the field, the lowest number seat (typically seat 1)." - https://www.rateyourseats.com/fenway-park/seating/seating-chart . This sentence is TRUNCATED IN THE SOURCE ITSELF (it stops after 'typically seat 1)' with no predicate), but 'go from right-to-left' can only mean numbering STARTS on the RIGHT, i.e. SEAT 1 ON THE RIGHT. *** CONSEQUENCE: THE SEAT-1 SIDE AT FENWAY PARK IS UNRESOLVED. *** The brief notes that where per-section question-and-answer text exists it beats the boilerplate - HERE NO SUCH PER-SECTION TEXT EXISTS. Statement (A) IS the boilerplate; it is byte-identical on all 25 pages checked and therefore carries no independent per-section authority, and the brief warns that this same boilerplate was correct on one half of the ballpark and wrong on the other at two parks already. Statement (B) is a hand-written park-specific sentence but is grammatically incomplete. NO OFFICIAL RED SOX SOURCE STATES A SEAT-1 RULE - the disability access guide, the netting page and the MLB.com Fenway guide are all silent on seat numbering. *** DO NOT EMIT SEAT-1-SIDE STATEMENTS FOR FENWAY PARK UNTIL A THIRD, PER-SECTION SOURCE IS OBTAINED. *** A wrong choice here inverts every seat-1 statement in the park, and at an irregular park where sections face many different directions the error would not be self-evident.
known_obstructions: FENWAY IS THE MOST OBSTRUCTION-PRONE PARK IN MLB AND THE OBSTRUCTIONS ARE STRUCTURAL, NOT INCIDENTAL. (1) GRANDSTAND SUPPORT POLES/BEAMS - the dominant issue. Zone page, verbatim: 'Support poles positioned throughout the sections can block views of different parts of the field, including home plate, the pitcher's mound, second base, or the outfield, depending on the seat location.' and 'support poles and tight seating layouts were common design features at the time and remain part of the Grandstand experience today.' - https://www.rateyourseats.com/fenway-park/seating/grandstand-seats . PER-SECTION DETAIL, verbatim: GS18 - 'Stay within 6 seats of the left aisle'; 'Seats closer to the right side of Grandstand 18 will have to contend with the support beam for a view of the batters box and pitchers mound'; 'There is a support beam which sits just 4 seats in from the right aisle'. GS20 - 'Eliminate viewing obstructions by sitting in Row 1'; 'The beam at the right side of Row 1 could not be in a worse place for those sitting near the right aisle.' GS15 - 'You will find some kind of frustrating obstruction in every row of Grandstand 15' except Row 1. GS1 - reviewers caution fans to 'Avoid the right side' due to beam obstructions. GS33 - rows 1-2 have clear sightlines while higher rows 'risk obstruction from support pillars'. *** NOTE THE PATTERN: at Fenway the beams are repeatedly described as being on the RIGHT SIDE of the grandstand sections. This is a per-seat, direction-dependent fact and it interacts directly with the UNRESOLVED seat-1 side above - if the seat-1 side is chosen wrongly, every 'avoid the right side' warning will be emitted against the wrong seat numbers. *** (2) PROTECTIVE NETTING - OFFICIAL, verbatim from the Red Sox: 'The protective netting at Fenway Park extends from Field Box Section 79 to Field Box Section 9.' with 'varying heights all the way around, approximately 12 feet, 8 inches above the playing field.' - https://www.mlb.com/redsox/ballpark/netting . RateYourSeats concurs at zone level, verbatim: 'All seats in these sections sit behind protective netting, which extends across the infield to help protect fans from foul balls.' - https://www.rateyourseats.com/fenway-park/seating/field-boxes . So FB9 through FB79 inclusive are behind netting; FB1-FB8, FB80-FB82 and all of RFB87-97 are NOT. (3) ANGLED SEATS RATHER THAN BLOCKED ONES - Right Field Boxes, verbatim: 'Because the sections are positioned down the first base line, many seats face toward the outfield rather than toward the infield. For example, seats in Section 5 look more directly toward right field, meaning fans often need to turn their body to follow the action around home plate.' - https://www.rateyourseats.com/fenway-park/seating/right-field-boxes . (4) HORNITOS CANTINA - verbatim: views 'are among the most limited in the ballpark', as 'pop-ups and high fly balls can disappear from view', because it sits 'behind the traditional Grandstand seating sections' with 'support poles'. (5) ROOF BOX ANGLE - verbatim: 'the angle toward home plate can feel steep and distant compared to other seating areas'. (6) NOT AN OBSTRUCTION BUT AFFECTS AVAILABILITY - the centre-field bleachers are tarped off during day games to form the batter's eye (Wikipedia: 'Center field contains bleachers that are tarped off during day games'), which is why Fenway has separate day and night capacities.
uncertain: SEAT-1 SIDE IS UNRESOLVED AND IS THE SINGLE HIGHEST-RISK ITEM IN THIS FILE. The per-section boilerplate says 'lower number seats are on the left' (25 pages, byte-identical) while the same site's seating-chart page says 'Seat Numbers at Fenway Park go from right-to-left'. These are opposites. No official Red Sox source addresses seat numbering at all. See 'seat1_side_verbatim'. RESOLUTION NEEDED BEFORE ANY SEAT-1 OUTPUT IS GENERATED.

MIXED NUMBERING SCHEMAS IN ONE PARK - CONFIG SCHEMA IMPACT, NOT JUST VALUES. The lower tiers sweep clockwise (first base -> home -> third base) but the Aura Pavilion Club, Pavilion Box, Pavilion Reserved and Roof Box tiers number OUTWARD FROM HOME PLATE BY PARITY (odd = first base line, even = third base line). A single park-wide direction scalar cannot express Fenway. The parity evidence is strong for PC (explicit statement plus two per-section pages) and for PR (explicit per-section side statements); for PB and RB it is INFERRED from two independent sun/shade sources plus the odd-only RB series, NOT from a direct parity statement. Confirm PB and RB parity directly before relying on it.

RIGHT FIELD BOX ORDER WITHIN THE SERIES IS UNKNOWN. RFB87-RFB97 are all 'down the first base line near right field', but no source found states whether RFB87 or RFB97 is the one nearer the infield. Both section pages returned identical generic zone text. Do not assume either ordering.

RIGHT FIELD BOX NUMBERING BREAKS THE BOWL SWEEP. RFB87-97 sit in right field beside the LOW-numbered Field Boxes yet carry numbers above FB82, which is at the opposite end of the park. Sections 83-86 are absent from the index entirely - no source explains the gap. Any code that infers position from magnitude will place these sections in left field.

GRANDSTAND BEHIND-HOME-PLATE SECTIONS ARE MEDIUM CONFIDENCE. GS18-GS20 is the recorded anchor, derived from the GS20 page placing that section behind home plate and bounded by 'Sections 1-6' (first base side) and 'Grandstand Sections 23-33' (third base side). No source names the grandstand home-plate range explicitly, so the true range may be wider (anywhere within GS7-GS22). The DIRECTION is high confidence; the exact numbers are not.

GRANDSTAND SECTION 1 HAS NO EXPLICIT LOCATION QUOTE. Its first-base/right-field placement is inferred from 'Sections 1-6 are covered but can still receive late afternoon sun' combined with the independently sourced fact that the first base side is the late-sun side. The GS1 page's own review block is the generic 'Grandstand Seats' review and names no field position. The inference is corroborated by every other tier in the park but is not directly quoted.

CAPACITY: FOUR FIGURES, NO TWO AGREE - 37,775 (MLB.com, March 2026), 37,755 night (Wikipedia), 37,673 night and 37,221 day (Ballparks of Baseball). Fenway genuinely has different day and night capacities because the centre-field bleachers are tarped for the batter's eye, so no single scalar is fully correct. 37,775 recommended as the only 2026-dated, club-family figure.

STALE SPONSOR LABELS IN THE TICKETING SOURCE - THREE CONFIRMED. (i) The RateYourSeats section INDEX prints 'State Street Pavilion Club 1-14' but the section pages it links to are headed 'Aura Pavilion Club 1-14', and the official Red Sox accessibility guide also says 'Aura Club' and 'Aura Pavilion'. The index label is STALE. (ii) The URL slug 'EMCC' is the legacy EMC Club; the area is now the Dell Technologies Club and its own review text calls the sections 'DTC 1-DTC 6'. (iii) The index prints bare 'Section PB1'-'Section PB10' for some pavilion boxes and 'Pavilion Box 11'-'Pavilion Box 14' for others, and 'Section GS1' / 'Section EMCC1' / 'Section PR16' for others still - the index's DISPLAY LABELS ARE INCONSISTENT even where the underlying identifiers are regular. The URL-slug identifiers recorded in 'sections' are the stable form; the display labels are not.

PAVILION RESERVED SECTION COUNT DISAGREES WITH ITSELF. The zone page says 'Pavilion Reserved seats are labeled Sections 15-20 on the seating chart' and describes 'Sections 16-20', but the section index lists ONLY PR15, PR16, PR18 and PR20 - PR17 and PR19 have no pages. Recorded as the four that exist. The parity model predicts 17 and 19 would be first-base-side sections; whether they exist and are simply missing from the index, or do not exist at all, is UNKNOWN.
LOGE BOX 156 IS ABSENT from the index (LB155 is followed directly by LB157). No source explains the gap. Recorded as absent; do not generate LB156.

ROOF BOX ROW COUNT IS INTERNALLY CONTRADICTORY: 'Each section includes eight rows labeled A through G' - A through G is seven letters. Either the count or the label range is wrong. Do not rely on either.

BULLPEN OWNERSHIP IS MEDIUM CONFIDENCE. RateYourSeats' editorial insight says 'The Visiting Team Bullpen is in Front of Bleachers Sections 42 and 43', while a FAN REVIEW on the Bleachers 40 page says 'Only handicapped row in front, then the Red Sox bullpen and the field.' The pairing (Red Sox pen nearer centre field, visitors' pen nearer the right field corner) rests partly on fan-supplied data. No official Red Sox source found states which pen is which.

ORIENTATION HAS ONLY ONE TEXTUAL SOURCE. Only Where's The Shade gives a compass word ('northeast'). Baseball Almanac's AL ballpark orientation page renders Fenway's value as a GRAPHIC only and could not be quoted. No source gives degrees. The 'northeast' claim is corroborated only indirectly, by sun/shade behaviour and by the Gate B / Gate E elevator geography in the official accessibility guide.

ACCESSIBLE SEATING HAS NO SECTION NUMBERS ANYWHERE. The official Red Sox guide names only broad AREAS ('Grandstands, Bleachers, Green Monster, Right Field Roof Deck, Loge Box, Field Box, Right Field Roof Box, Aura Club, Aura Pavilion, Dell Technologies Club'). Per-section accessible locations and accessible-row label conventions are UNKNOWN. Also note https://www.mlb.com/redsox/ballpark/accessibility returns 404; the live path is /ballpark/disability-access-guide.

MLB.COM SEATING-MAP PAGE IS DEAD: https://www.mlb.com/redsox/ballpark/seating-map returns 404, so no official section index could be obtained. EVERY section identifier in 'sections' comes from RateYourSeats alone and is UNCORROBORATED BY AN OFFICIAL SOURCE, except the Field Box numbers 9 and 79 (netting page) and the broad area names (accessibility guide). The Field Box series in particular - 82 consecutive sections - has no official confirmation of its extent.
